claims.text: The target alloy has the nominal composition Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3.
The as-built additively manufactured alloy has an fcc matrix.
The as-built fcc matrix is homogeneous.
The as-built alloy contains minimal pre-existing oxidation or intergranular oxide phases.
Elevated-temperature exposure to an oxidizing atmosphere accelerates oxygen diffusion along grain boundaries.
Oxygen diffuses preferentially along grain boundaries rather than through the fcc matrix at elevated temperature.
Grain-boundary oxygen ingress produces continuous, brittle oxide films.
The proposed grain-boundary oxide films are primarily enriched in Al, Cr, and Ti oxides.
Continuous grain-boundary oxide films weaken cohesion between grains.
A critical amount of intergranular oxidation initiates crack nucleation and propagation under service stresses.
Loss of grain-boundary cohesion can culminate in catastrophic intergranular failure.
Reducing oxygen availability moderates oxide formation and delays degradation.
Oxidizing exposure will increase grain-boundary oxide-film thickness relative to the unexposed baseline.
Oxidizing exposure will increase the connectivity of the intergranular oxide network relative to the unexposed baseline.
Oxidizing exposure will reduce tensile strength or fracture toughness relative to the unexposed baseline.
Low-oxygen or reducing exposure will produce less oxidation and mechanical degradation than oxidizing exposure.
The proposed mechanism applies above approximately 700°C.
The oxidizing regime is defined as an oxygen partial pressure at or above that of air, approximately 0.21 atm.
Compositional variation and additive-manufacturing microstructural heterogeneity may alter oxidation kinetics and the critical oxide thickness for failure.
